properties.GEOL_DESC: Now known as the Shoemaker Impact Crater. Two concentric rings at 30 km and 12 km diameter about a central granitoid uplift. Age poorly constrained — possibly between 1300 Ma and 568 Ma
properties.GEOSOURCE: Carter, JD, 1987, Important geological localities beyond the Perth Region.., Geological Society of Australia, p269

properties.GEOL_DESC: Turbiditic sedimentary structures in arkosic sandstones of the Doolgunna Formation; rip-up clasts, basal scours, convolute bedding and cross bedding
properties.GEOSOURCE: Carter, JD, 1987, Important geological localities beyond the Perth Region.., Geological Society of Australia, p118

properties.GEOL_DESC: Probable astrobleme, 9 km across. Central peak of deformed Aptian (125–113 Ma) Samuel Formation sandstone; the age of the impact is therefore after the deposition of Samuel Formation
properties.GEOSOURCE: Carter, JD, 1987, Important geological localities beyond the Perth Region.., Geological Society of Australia, p269
properties.REMARKS: Mentioned by Shoemaker et al., in 1985 - short article in Meteoritics, v20. No.4.

properties.GEOL_DESC: Dinosaur footprints in Broome Sandstone, low-tide exposure; large tridactyl, theropod and sauropod footoprints identified; plant macrofossils
properties.GEOSOURCE: Carter, JD, 1987, Important geological localities beyond the Perth Region.., Geological Society of Australia, p263

properties.GEOL_DESC: Impact crater, possibly Eocene in age (astrobleme), approximately 5–6 km across, deforming sandstone units of the Paleoproterozoic Pentecost Formation
properties.GEOSOURCE: Carter, JD, 1987, Important geological localities beyond the Perth Region.., Geological Society of Australia, p265
properties.REMARKS: Milton, DJ and MacDonald, FA, 2005. Goat Paddock, Western Australia:An impact crater near the simple-complex transition. Aust Journal of Earth Sciences vol 52, p 689–697.

properties.GEOL_DESC: Late Frasnian (Devonian) platform facies of the Pillara Formation with narrow reef-margin and/or reef-flat subfacies rimming back-reef subfacies; Napier Formation marginal-slope limestone; neptunian dykes

properties.GEOL_DESC: Devonian reef complex; stromatolite bioherm development on pinnacle reefs; internationally important example of Devonian reef sedimentation, paleontology and paleoecology

properties.GEOL_DESC: Four large stromatolite and receptaculitid–sponge–microbial bioherms, part of the Devonian reef complex

properties.GEOL_DESC: Karst geomorphology; natural tunnel (700 m long) formed in the Napier Formation, Devonian reef complex

properties.REMARKS: Playford et al., 2009, GSWA Bulletin 145, p334

properties.GEOL_DESC: Marginal-slope facies of the Devonian Napier Formation; reef complex, includes debris flow deposits and large allochthonous reef blocks; stromatolite bioherm development; early Permian subglacial karst depression

properties.GEOL_DESC: Miocene lamproite vent; 200 m diameter circular ridge with 15 m depression; pyroclastic rocks are intruded by sills of richterite–phlogopite–leucite composition. Volcanic structures in tuff include dropstones, cross bedding, slumping and lahars

properties.GEOL_DESC: Hill 90 m high with central magmatic core of coarse phlogopite–leucite lamproite; thin sills of olivine–leucite lamprolite; well-bedded 'sandy' tuff; central core has columnar jointing
properties.GEOSOURCE: Carter, JD, 1987, Important geological localities beyond the Perth Region.., Geological Society of Australia, p258, Perrigo/Halligan
properties.REMARKS: Detailed geology description, photographs and sketches in GSWA Bulletin 132 by Jacques A.L.

properties.GEOL_DESC: River gorge exposure along Lennard River; Devonian reef complexes; Fore-reef and marginal-slope limestones, platform facies, conglomerates, breccias, neptunian dykes

properties.GEOL_DESC: Astrobleme caused by oblique impact; upthrust plates of quartzite radiating from 500 m wide central dome; shatter cones; aged between 900–600 Ma

properties.REMARKS: Guidebook to the Geology of Rottnest Island by Phillip Playford available fron Geological Survey of Western Australia

properties.GEOL_DESC: Geomorphology; beehive weathering in Devonian sandstone, similar to the Bungle Bungles

properties.GEOL_DESC: Folded (anticlinal) Cenozoic stratigraphy; type sections of the Mandu and Tulki Limestones, evidence of shallowing upwards carbonate succession, folding due to collision and continued interaction with Indonesia

properties.REMARKS: Australia goes it alone by AE Cockbain 2014, ps 13–14
